entries.name: Mobile-VideoGPT
entries.summary: Combines efficient spatial and temporal encoders with attention-based frame selection and a small language model, targeting lower-cost video question answering and edge-device deployment.
entries.architecture: CLIP-B/16 extracts spatial features from all sampled frames. Attention-based scoring selects salient frames for VideoMamba-M temporal encoding. Efficient Token Projectors refine features, reduce tokens through pooling, and add positional context before spatial and temporal representations are fused. A Qwen2.5 small language model consumes the compact visual-language sequence and generates responses to video questions.
entries.temporal_modeling: Frame scoring limits temporal-encoder computation to selected observations. VideoMamba captures motion context, while projected spatial and temporal tokens preserve complementary evidence for the decoder.
entries.training: Image-projector and video-projector warm-up keep pretrained encoders and the language model frozen. Instruction tuning then trains both projectors and applies LoRA to the language model using mixed image and video conversation data.

entries.name: Slow-Fast Video MLLM
entries.summary: Keeps detailed visual evidence available through cross-attention while compressed preview tokens enter self-attention, allowing instruction-aware video reading inside a hybrid language decoder.
entries.architecture: ConvNeXt-XXL and a projector form slow visual features. Strided sampling and temporal pooling create compressed fast tokens concatenated with text for Qwen2-7B self-attention. Selected decoder layers add cross-attention from text to uncompressed slow features. A dynamic gate and warm-up factor control this residual pathway, preserving detail without loading every visual token into self-attention.
entries.temporal_modeling: Fast tokens give a broad temporal preview, while text-conditioned cross-attention reads detailed slow evidence. Temporal pooling controls preview length without discarding the accessible slow representation.
entries.training: Cross-attention projections inherit language self-attention weights where applicable, with a warm-up gate stabilizing integration. Visual-language alignment precedes mixed image, video, and text instruction tuning, teaching the hybrid decoder to select useful fine-grained evidence.

entries.name: ReKV
entries.summary: ReKV is a training-free inference method that stores streaming video KV states outside GPU memory and retrieves relevant states when a question arrives.
entries.architecture: A pretrained decoder-based Video-LLM encodes the stream once using sliding-window attention. Video KV states leaving the active window are offloaded to RAM or disk. A query selects relevant cached keys and values through cosine-similarity retrieval, accelerated by compressed representations. Retrieved states return to GPU memory and serve as context for autoregressive answer generation, avoiding repeated video encoding.
entries.temporal_modeling: The sliding window captures local temporal context during encoding; indexed historical KV blocks retain evidence from earlier video regions for query-conditioned retrieval and reuse.
entries.training: No additional training is required. ReKV changes attention, cache storage, and retrieval during inference while reusing pretrained Video-LLM weights. Its experiments attach the method to existing video-capable backbones; it is a cache-management method rather than a separately trained model.

entries.name: StreamChat (Xiong et al.)
entries.summary: Xiong et al.'s StreamChat is a training-free memory orchestration framework, combining hierarchical video evidence and dialogue history for streaming understanding and multi-round interaction.
entries.architecture: Selective Frame Stacking encodes and buffers informative visual features. Memory Formation organizes them into recent short-term memory, a long-term memory tree, and a dialogue memory. Contextual Summarization retrieves question-relevant evidence and constructs context for an existing MLLM. Parallel scheduling separates frame processing from interaction, so the system can keep accumulating memory while answering user questions.
entries.temporal_modeling: Short-term memory tracks ongoing events; hierarchical long-term memory compresses earlier video. Retrieved dialogue history supports continuity across multiple questions about different temporal regions.
entries.training: No additional training is required. The framework reuses pretrained visual-language models and embedding-based retrieval, introducing storage, compression, summarization, and scheduling around them. This memory system and StreamBench contribution are distinct from Liu et al.'s separately trained StreamChat cross-attention architecture.

entries.name: TimeRefine
entries.summary: TimeRefine improves existing temporal-grounding Video-LLMs by generating coarse boundaries followed by iterative offsets, supplemented with an auxiliary head that penalizes localization error.
entries.architecture: The method retains a host Video-LLM's visual encoder, connector, and language decoder, demonstrated with VTimeLLM and VTG-LLM. It reformats the decoder output as an initial temporal interval followed by refinement predictions and offsets. An auxiliary regression head supplements the next-token head during training. The last interval and offsets yield the final localized segment, adding temporal precision without replacing the host architecture.
entries.temporal_modeling: Iterative residual offsets refine coarse predictions. The auxiliary L1 objective distinguishes near-miss boundaries from distant errors, which ordinary token classification does not directly express.
entries.training: This method requires training. Grounding QA targets are converted into refinement sequences using progressively decreasing timestamp noise; non-grounding targets remain unchanged. Apply the host model's original training data and settings while adding next-token and auxiliary regression supervision.

entries.name: StreamMeCo
entries.summary: StreamMeCo compresses an agent's long-term memory graph and prioritizes recent relevant evidence, reducing retrieval cost for streaming video understanding without changing the visual-language backbone.
entries.architecture: Applied to a memory-based video agent M3-Agent, StreamMeCo operates after perceptual evidence has entered a graph. Edge-free Minmax Sampling (EMsampling) compresses isolated nodes, while Edge-aware Weighting Pruning (EWpruning) removes less useful connected nodes using importance and similarity signals. Time-decay Memory Retrieval (TMR) reweights query matches with temporal decay. The retained and retrieved graph evidence then supports the host agent's language-model reasoning.
entries.temporal_modeling: Timestamp-aware decay favors recent relevant memories during retrieval, while graph compression limits growing historical storage and preserves important entity-linked evidence from earlier observations.
entries.training: The proposed compression and retrieval procedures require no new model training. They operate on memory graphs produced by an existing agent, with sampling, pruning, and decay parameters selected in evaluation. The contribution belongs to the agent memory layer rather than a new video encoder.

technical_sources.title: StreamMeCo: Long-Term Agent Memory Compression for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding

entries.name: FlashVID
entries.summary: FlashVID compresses video tokens without training, combining attention-and-diversity selection with tree-based spatiotemporal merging to retain representative evidence under limited language-model input budgets.
entries.architecture: A pretrained Video-LLM's visual encoder first produces frame tokens. Attention and Diversity-based Token Selection chooses informative, diverse representatives using calibrated attention and feature diversity. Tree-based Spatiotemporal Token Merging then groups redundant features through constrained redundancy trees spanning space and time. The compressed token sequence enters the original connector and LLM, allowing the unchanged backbone to process more frames within its token budget.
entries.temporal_modeling: Merging considers cross-frame spatial changes instead of matching only identical positions. Tree depth and breadth constraints limit temporal span and preserve local video dynamics.
entries.training: No additional training is required. Selection and merging use existing visual features and attention signals while preserving pretrained weights. The paper evaluates the method with LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, and Qwen2.5-VL, illustrating a reusable inference module rather than a new checkpoint.

entries.name: SlowFast-LLaVA
entries.summary: SlowFast-LLaVA extends an image-trained LLaVA-NeXT model to video without fine-tuning, combining sparse detailed frames with dense spatially pooled frames under a fixed token budget.
entries.architecture: The existing image encoder extracts features independently for uniformly sampled frames. A slow pathway keeps relatively few frames with detailed spatial tokens. A fast pathway retains many more frames but applies stronger spatial pooling. Their aggregated visual representations are provided to the unchanged LLaVA-NeXT connector and decoder with a video-oriented prompt, trading spatial detail against temporal coverage explicitly.
entries.temporal_modeling: Dense fast-path frames capture changes between sparsely sampled slow-path frames. Temporal evidence comes from ordered multiframe inputs rather than a separately trained video encoder.
entries.training: No additional training is required. The method reuses image-trained LLaVA-NeXT weights and adjusts sampling, feature pooling, token aggregation, and prompting. It differs from the later trained Slow-Fast Video MLLM, whose decoder includes a separate cross-attention route.
